name: Compromise and Revocation Drill
description: Scheduled drill: simulate a key compromise, execute revocation, verify consumers get the update.
purpose: Ensure the team can detect, respond to, and recover from a key compromise event by running scheduled revocation drills that test the full incident response chain.
acceptanceCriteria: Compromise drill is scheduled quarterly and documented as an on-call procedure.
Drill simulates a key compromise event (root key, targets key, or timestamp key).
Revocation procedure is executed: key rotation, metadata re-signing, Rekor entry invalidation.
Consumer-side verification confirms that old signatures are rejected and new metadata is accepted.
Drill participants are briefed beforehand and debriefed afterward with a runbook update.
Drill results are documented with time-to-detect, time-to-respond, and improvement actions.
Drill runbook is version-controlled and reviewed after each drill.
